system.name: 3C 273
system.description: The first quasar ever optically identified and the brightest in the sky, 2.4 billion light-years away. It blazes with the luminosity of four trillion Suns as a supermassive black hole consumes surrounding gas at a ferocious rate.

3c273-bh.name: 3C 273
3c273-bh.description: A quasar powered by a 886-million-solar-mass black hole surrounded by a blazing accretion disk. First identified in 1963, 3C 273 was the first object recognised as being at a cosmological distance — its enormous redshift revealed it lay billions of light-years away. Its luminosity varies on timescales of weeks, implying the energy-producing region is only light-weeks across.
3c273-bh.funFact: Despite being 2.4 billion light-years away, 3C 273 is visible through a modest amateur telescope — it outshines the entire Milky Way by a factor of over 100.
